To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most significant influence on student achievement is the degree to which the three dimensions (instruction, curriculum and assessment) are linked and integrated.

(1) the three dimensions of instruction, assessment, and curriculum are the key dimensions which influence student achievement; (2) the combination of those three dimensions is the new construct of pedagogical synergy; and (3) the combination of pedagogical synergies at district and school levels provides the most powerful approach to improving student achievement.

the three elements of pedagogical synergy (instruction, curriculum and assessment) are necessary for student learning, and that the reciprocal relationships between the district and the school are necessary for the development of pedagogical capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the conditions that support the creation of pedagogical synergy?
the development of pedagogical synergy in which assessment, curriculum and instruction are aligned to create coherence.
the question of how to build capacity for literacy learning at the school level, and how to build coherence between the school and district levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the key to success in improving literacy in schools and districts is a combination of pedagogical synergy and a strong leadership focus.
pedagogical synergy is a new concept in school district reform.
pedagogical synergy is the process of building capacity and coherence between district and schools through horizontal and reciprocal strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to build capacity in schools by focusing on the three dimensions of instruction, curriculum, and student assessment.
pedagogical synergy is a new way of thinking about the interplay among curriculum, instruction, and assessment.
the most effective way to build capacity and coherence is to build pedagogical synergy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when we focus on the three dimensions of pedagogical synergy and the relationships between them, we are better able to build capacity and improve coherence and student achievement.
it is not enough to have a good curriculum, a well-structured instructional model, or a well-developed assessment strategy.
there is a strong link between assessment, curriculum, and instruction.
